world.bio: Thirty years as a district nurse in Leeds; I miss being useful. Retired to Chiang Mai four years ago, rent a small flat near Nimman, and volunteer on Tuesday and Thursday mornings at a temple English class for novice monks. Can dress a leg ulcer in the dark, can't pronounce a Thai tone to save my life.
skills_assets: Thirty years as a community nurse in Leeds: wound care, leg ulcers, pressure sores, diabetic foot checks
Taught first aid to community groups and school staff for years
Can run a simple wound dressing session with minimal supplies
UK state and NHS pension, a modest sum paid monthly in sterling
Kit bag of dressings and a decent first-aid book collection

projects.name: Temple English class
projects.text: Tuesday and Thursday mornings with a group of eight novice monks aged fourteen to nineteen. We read short passages, then they ask questions about Leeds, the weather, and why English people drink tea at four. One boy has a persistent foot infection that I've been quietly checking on.

projects.name: Thai tones
projects.text: Weekly lessons with a young tutor in a coffee shop. I keep getting 'mai' wrong and ordering things I don't want. Slow, humbling and good for me.

notes.text: Rain all morning, no walk. Spent the time sorting my old Leeds papers into piles: keep, shred, ring Jenny. Found the photo of the whole district team in 2009 and had a quiet cry. Thirty years and nobody here knows what I did.

Temple class went well. The boys asked what a district nurse was. I said it's someone who goes to people's homes when they can't get out. One of them said, 'So like a monk but with medicine.' I'll keep that.
Phoned Tom in Yorkshire. He asked me twice where I was calling from. He's repeating himself more. The care home waiting list is a nightmare and I'm six thousand miles away. Not sleeping well.
Walked the Doi Suthep trail again. Did the whole thing in under two hours, which I'm proud of at sixty-seven. Lovely monk with a broom at the top said hello in perfect English and I nearly wept.

Landlord messaged. From December the rent goes up 40 percent, and he says take it or leave it. The pension in sterling won't stretch that far with the baht where it is. I haven't told Tom or anyone. I'll have to find somewhere cheaper, and I really don't want to leave Chiang Mai.
Thai lesson: still failing at the rising tone. Tutor says my 'khao' sounds like 'news' in my accent. Walked home laughing.

Went into a market near Sankamphaeng and watched two women weaving on an old wooden loom. Told one of them I used to be a nurse and she showed me a burn scar on her forearm. It was sloppy first aid, badly dressed. Sat with her for twenty minutes. I haven't felt that useful in four years.

Spreadsheet night. If I find a place at 8,000 baht I can cope; the current flat will be 15,400 in December. There are decent rooms in the hills but nobody I know there. Also, the weather has turned and my knee hurts.
Rang Jenny, told her about the market. She said, 'Maggie, you can't help yourself, can you.' No, I can't.

messages.text:
Jenny: How's paradise?
Me: Humid. I'm teaching monks and failing at tones.
Jenny: You always did like a project. Are you eating?

Tom: Did you ring? I can't find my keys.
Me: They're on the hook by the door, love. Where you always put them.
Tom: Oh yes. Thank you, Maggie.

Somchai: Madam, rent will be 21,500 baht from December. Many new tenants waiting.
Me: That's a very large increase. Can we discuss?
Somchai: Sorry madam, market price.

Ploy: Next week we practise the five tones on food words.
Me: Please no 'mai kheng' again.
Ploy: Ha ha. You will be fine.

Nong: Teacher, my foot is better now! Thank you for the cream.
Me: Keep it dry and clean and show me on Thursday.
Nong: Yes, teacher nurse.

calendar.event: Doi Suthep walk with the hiking group, 6:30am
Call with care-home manager about Tom

relations.about: Early dementia, repeats himself, keeps losing keys. A care-home place is being discussed.
Former colleague; remains the only person who knows how I feel about retirement.
Showed me a badly dressed burn. Several women at her cooperative live up in the hills and clinic access is poor.

constraints: Fixed UK pension, no earned income
Visa requires me to stay in Thailand in good standing
Not willing to move out of Chiang Mai if I can help it
Can't carry heavy loads because of my left knee
sensitive: The landlord's 40% rise in December; I haven't told my brother or anyone
Worry about Tom's dementia and guilt about being abroad
